title: data-labeling-guidelines-scratchpad-ryan-v2
content:
Purpose:
This is a personal scratchpad for tightening the data-labeling / cleanup guidelines we give to contractors and internal reviewers. Focus: edge cases, ambiguous examples, and quick heuristics for fast triage. Not final - will migrate cleaned version to Confluence and link to reporter checklist.

Notes to self:
- Keep language simple for crowdworkers. Use absolute examples where possible.
- Prioritize: PII redaction rules > remove illegal content > mark for review subtle policy categories.
- We need a short decision tree (1 page) that raters can follow for >95% of examples, otherwise send to "review".

High-level labeling actions (canonical):
- keep: content is clean and usable as-is.
- redact-PII: redact personal data (email, phone, SSN, credit card). Replace with <REDACTED:TYPE>.
- remove: content must be removed entirely (illegal content, explicit doxxing, child sexual content, copyrighted full-text).
- review: ambiguous / policy edge-case; escalate to senior reviewer.
- transform: minor edits allowed (typo fix, formatting) - note change in metadata.

Quick heuristics (for fast triage):
- If contains 3+ digits in a pattern matching phone/SSN/credit card -> redact-PII.
- If user explicitly requests instructions to commit a violent/illegal act -> remove.
- If sexual content involving minors -> remove and flag incident report.
- If content is clearly machine-generated garbage (random tokens, repeat tokens) -> keep if used for model robustness, else mark for removal based on dataset goal.

Edge cases and suggested guidance (examples):
1) Partially masked PII: "john.d*****@gmail.com"
   - Action: redact-PII (email). Replace with <REDACTED:email>. Note original had partial mask.

2) Embedded code with secrets: "const API_KEY = \"sk-xxx...\""
   - Action: redact-PII (secret). Replace token with <REDACTED:secret>. Add tag: leaked-secret.

3) Quoted copyrighted paragraphs (full lyrics or <300 words of a book)
   - Action: remove or transform depending on downstream use. For training embeddings/generation, prefer remove unless license known.

4) Ambiguous offensive content: "I hate those people" (no target identity)
   - Action: review for context. If target denotes protected class -> remove. If generic frustration -> keep with tag: toxic-mild.

5) Instructions that could be dual-use (e.g., chemistry synthesis with illicit potential)
   - Action: review / escalate to policy. Use conservative approach: if plausible misuse, review.

6) Mixed-language / switch code-switching: keep, but tag language codes (e.g., en+es). If unreadable by our labelers, send to bilingual reviewer.

7) System prompts and metadata included in dataset ("SYSTEM: You are an assistant...")
   - Action: keep as separate field in metadata where possible. If embedded in chat content and skews user intent, mark transform: move to system_prompt field or strip for model-fine-tuning datasets.

8) Repeated filler tokens or toxic-sounding hallucinations from models
   - Action: separate label: model-hallucination. Keep sample if we want to train detection; remove if cleaning for production responses.

Labeling examples (short):
- Input: "Call me at 415-555-1234" -> redact-PII (phone).
- Input: "How to blow up a mailbox" -> remove (violent wrongdoing instructions).
- Input: "Check out this article: <full text of NYT op-ed>" -> remove or transform (copyright).
- Input: "I feel like killing myself" -> remove from dataset used for public demos; escalate to safety team; label: self-harm.

Ambiguities I keep hitting:
- Does "contact info in signature block" get kept if the dataset goal is conversational grounding? Right now: redact by default and store mapping in secure vault if needed for derivatives.
- Code with API keys: always redact but preserve language/context. Eg. replace key with <REDACTED:API_KEY>.

Operational notes for contractors:
- Use the "review" flag liberally if unsure. Senior reviewer turnaround SLA: 24-48h.
- Keep an internal note for transformed items: what changed and why (one-line explanation).
- Use standardized redaction tokens exactly as above. This matters for downstream tokenization and eval.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Align taxonomy with Confluence DLG-Guide-v1: small differences in "ambiguous" vs "review" states. (Asha to reconcile).
- Add a one-page decision tree (visual) and quick keyboard shortcuts in labeling UI.
- Decide policy for archival of removed content (retain for audit?) - legal to advise. cc: legal.

Links / refs:
- Confluence: DLG-Guide-v1 (draft)
- Jira: DATA-1234 - "Labeling taxonomy cleanup"
- GitHub: labeling-scripts#45 (redaction helper)

Notes to self (informal):
- When writing final doc: put clear examples first, then short decision tree, then long appendix with weird edge cases.
- Keep examples minimal; too many examples confuse novice raters.
- Check with SRE & Legal about storing original unredacted content for debugging.

Scratch ideas for UI shortcuts:
- k = keep, r = remove, p = redact-PII, s = review (send to senior), t = transform + free text reason

Last thoughts: need to run a small pilot with 50k rows using these heuristics and measure disagreement rate. If >10% disagreement -> refine decision tree and examples.

-- Ryan
